text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions raised with a central dimple, and have you noticed any new lesions appearing over the past few days?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do any of the lesions have a white, cheesy core that can be expressed, and have you noticed if scratching them has led to new clusters of bumps appearing nearby?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for molluscum contagiosum, a common viral skin infection in children. I will now confirm the diagnosis and prepare the treatment plan. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
